transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-28
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood Solutions); Marcus Chen (Sable Head Eng), Rina Alvarez (Sable CISO), Ethan Boyle (Platform PM), Sofia Marin (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick intake to map hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) to Sable's security/regulatory controls. Focus on GDPR data residency, HIPAA footprint (they have a small wealth-health product), audit log retention and redaction, KMS/customer-managed keys, and ability to lock models/traffic to EU region only. Action items and a security deep-dive were agreed.

Topics covered (auto): hosting modes, encryption/KMS, logging and audit trails, data residency/geofencing, SOC2/BAA, integration and rollback policies, sample throughput and pricing drivers.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Monroe: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Marcus Chen: Marcus here, hi.
[00:06] Rina Alvarez: Rina, hi.
[00:07] Ethan Boyle: Ethan here.
[00:08] Sofia Marin: Sofia, compliance.
[00:10] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood, SE.
[00:12] Jordan Li: Jordan, solutions.
[00:15] Alex Monroe: Cool. High level, Sable is evaluating where to run LLM inference for our new wealth assistant — hosted for speed to market, Dedicated for predictable throughput, Private for their regulated clients. We want to map controls and identify gaps. Marcus, can you give us the current stack and constraints?
[00:30] Marcus Chen: Sure. We run mostly on PublicCloudZ in eu-west-1 for EU customers, some us-east for US. Our user data is strongly partitioned by customer region. For the wealth assistant, PII like SSN-like identifiers, account balances, and some health-related notes for a subset — so we need HIPAA-level controls for that subset and GDPR. We're trying to avoid spinning up full on-prem just for this but we do need strong attestations.
[01:02] Alex Monroe: Got it. When you say HIPAA-level for subset — do you plan to route that traffic to a separate instance or scrub before send?
[01:12] Marcus Chen: Ideally separate routing. We don't want sensitive records hitting hosted unless covered by a BAA and customer-managed keys, region lock.
[01:20] Rina Alvarez: Also audit windows — regulators want 7 years in some cases, and we have internal policy for 10 years. But we also have retention minimization for GDPR, so there's a tension between long audit trails and minimization.
[01:34] Priya Nair: Yeah, that tension is common. Redwood has configurable log retention, and for Hosted we can provide token-level cost/lats but logs by default are aggregated. For Dedicated and Private, customers can retain raw logs longer and also choose redaction layers.
[01:51] Ethan Boyle: Can you clarify what "raw logs" include? We need request payloads, model prompts, completions for QA and e-discovery.
[01:58] Jordan Li: Good question. For Hosted, by default we keep telemetry, errors, latency, and a sampled subset of prompts for 30 days. For Dedicated, you can set the retention window and choose to collect full request/response logs to your log sink; for Private, everything stays in customer VPC and you control the sink. There are redaction hooks as well.
[02:22] Sofia Marin: When you say redaction hooks, is that pre-ingest or post-ingest? We need deterministic PII masking before storage for EU users.
[02:31] Priya Nair: We support both. You can do client-side masking or use our pre-ingest plugins that run inside the runtime and can redact fields before storing. For Hosted we run the plugin in our control plane; for Private it runs in customer infra so data never leaves. Note: plugin correctness is customer responsibility; Redwood provides policies and a regex-based starter pack.
[02:56] Rina Alvarez: About keys — can Redwood use our KMS or do we have to use Redwood-managed keys? What's the story for HSM?
[03:05] Alex Monroe: Short answer: we offer customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we offer CMKs using vendor KMS (e.g., AWS KMS) with customer key options when on dedicated plans. HSM-backed keys can be supported on Private deployments — we integrate with customer HSMs or bring-your-own via standard APIs.
[03:28] Marcus Chen: So for Hosted there's still some Redwood control plane involvement even with CMKs? Could that be a compliance blocker?
[03:35] Priya Nair: For Hosted, the control plane is managed by Redwood. With CMKs we can encrypt at rest and the key usage events still show up in your KMS logs. But there's a potential need for Private if your auditors mandate zero Redwood admin access to key ops. We can outline the exact separation for auditors.
[03:52] Ethan Boyle: Region locking — can we ensure inference workloads never leave eu-west-1 for EU customers?
[03:59] Jordan Li: Yes, we have region pinning. For Hosted we currently have region isolation options: EU-only hosting on our eu cluster with data routing policies. For Dedicated you allocate capacity in the region(s) you want. For Private it's deployed into your region. The caveat: fallback policies — if you enable cross-region fallback for availability, that may move traffic. We can set strict routing policies to avoid that.
[04:25] Marcus Chen: What about KV cache and prefix caching? If we have cached tokens that are customer-specific, are those logs considered PII?
[04:34] Priya Nair: KV entries are ephemeral by design but for Dedicated and Private you can control whether caches are persisted to disk. We also provide options to scrub or encrypt cached keys. By default, cached entries do not include raw PII; they are embeddings or token indices, but we recommend treating them as sensitive for regulated workloads.
[04:55] Rina Alvarez: SOC2/BAA — do you provide a BAA? SOC2 Type II?
[05:02] Alex Monroe: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II reports; we can sign BAAs for customers that need HIPAA coverage. I'll attach the SOC2 report and our BAA template. Note: BAAs typically require dedicated or private deployments for full coverage on your side's expectations, but we'll walk through specifics.
[05:18] Sofia Marin: Can you support granular RBAC and SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning? Auditors look for that.
[05:25] Jordan Li: Absolutely. SSO via SAML/OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC with per-team policies are in the console. For Private, that integrates with your IdP in your VPC.
[05:36] Ethan Boyle: Pricing sensitivity — we care about unit economics. Are there levers to trade latency for cost?
[05:41] Priya Nair: Yes — batching, async inference for non-real-time flows, quantized model variants, and Dedicated autoscaling can reduce cost. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations on quantization and batching thresholds. There's a tradeoff: batching hurts tail latencies but improves tokens/sec cost.
[05:58] Marcus Chen: For our wealth assistant we need sub-200ms median inference for simple prompts, longer for long-form. Can Dedicated get us that reliably?
[06:07] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated pools pinned to specific GPU types can meet sub-200ms medians for shorter sequences; it depends on model size, sequence length and batch policy. We'll model your expected QPS and prompt sizes in the sizing exercise.
[06:25] Rina Alvarez: Logging again — when you ship logs to a sink, can you apply redaction transforms server-side and still keep an audit of the redaction decisions? Auditors want to see who redacted what and why.
[06:39] Jordan Li: We capture redaction audit trails: metadata records that a redaction occurred, the rule or plugin id, timestamp, and operator id, but not the original redacted text. The audit trail lives separately and can be pushed to your SIEM.
[06:54] Sophia / Sofia Marin: (overlap) good
[07:00] Marcus Chen: About e-discovery — in a subpoena could we get a path to reconstitute older content?
[07:08] Priya Nair: For Hosted, reconstitution is limited if you didn't retain raw payloads; for Dedicated/Private, if you configure long-term retention you could reconstruct. Also we support escrowed backups for legal holds on Dedicated.
[07:26] Rina Alvarez: What about model updates and drift — we need a change log and ability to freeze model versions for audit.
[07:35] Alex Monroe: Redwood supports model version pinning and rollout policies — you can freeze a model version and control rollouts via A/B and canary. The console stores metadata on rollouts as part of the audit trail.
[07:48] Ethan Boyle: Are third-party models allowed? We want to experiment with open weights and some in-house models.
[07:54] Jordan Li: Yes. Hosted has a curated catalog of verified open models. Dedicated and Private let you bring-your-own model weights; for Private, the weights never leave your infra. We run a lightweight onboarding to validate performance.
[08:08] Marcus Chen: Let's talk about timelines. If we choose Dedicated, how long to provision a cluster and get to production?
[08:15] Priya Nair: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 4-6 weeks — includes capacity provisioning, network setup (VPC peering or private link), and baseline benchmarks. Private deployments can take longer depending on your infra team and security reviews — 6-12 weeks is common. Hosted can be immediate with sandbox access.
[08:31] Rina Alvarez: One more: can we get a compliance pack for auditors — network diagrams, personnel access lists, SOC2, encryption diagrams?
[08:39] Alex Monroe: Yes we have a compliance pack. I'll assemble for you: SOC2, vendor attestations, network diagrams for Dedicated, and an initial control-mapping doc that maps Redwood controls to typical FINRA/regulatory controls.
[08:52] Marcus Chen: On the technical side, Priya, can you outline how traffic is routed when we have private VPC and shared model runtime? Specifically, we want to ensure the inference plane doesn't touch public internet and logging is over private link.
[09:03] Priya Nair: For Private, the runtime is in your VPC; data flows internal only. For Dedicated, we provide options: VPC peering, PrivateLink endpoints, or dedicated interconnect. Logs can be pushed to your cloud logging endpoint over private networking. Hosted offers PrivateLink for enterprise plans so traffic doesn't traverse public net.
[09:25] Marcus Chen: There was mention of control plane vs data plane separation earlier — can you detail what the control plane can see?
[09:32] Jordan Li: Control plane monitors health, billing telemetry, and scheduling metadata. It does not see decrypted payloads when customer-managed keys are enforced on Private. On Hosted with Redwood-managed keys, the control plane may have access to telemetry that includes truncated prompt samples if enabled. We'll include a clear diagram in the pack.
[09:52] Rina Alvarez: Is there a way to do in-line DPI for PII detection that blocks send if PII found?
[09:58] Priya Nair: You can set pre-ingest validators that return a block or transform decision. On Hosted, it's a managed feature; on Private it's deployed in your infra. Blocking increases latency and error surface but is doable.
[10:14] Ethan Boyle: For the performance benchmarks, can we run a pilot with our sample prompt set?
[10:19] Alex Monroe: Yes. Typical pilot: 2-week Dedicated trial or 1-week Hosted sandbox with synthetic load. We'll run your prompt set and return token-level lat and cost breakdowns.
[10:28] Marcus Chen: Any big gotchas between Dedicated and Private other than control?
[10:33] Priya Nair: Main differences: ownership of infra (you vs Redwood), patching cadence, and networking complexity. Private gives you full control and isolation at the cost of ops burden. Dedicated hits a middle ground: isolated pools but Redwood still manages the runtime.
[10:48] Sofia Marin: For GDPR subject access requests, can you extract user request history for a given user id across logs and models?
[10:56] Jordan Li: If you retain per-request identifiers and raw payloads, yes. We provide APIs to query per-user logs; for Hosted, it's subject to retention policy and sampling. For Dedicated/Private you can enable full tracing.
[11:10] Marcus Chen: Do you support data residency for backups and snapshots?
[11:14] Alex Monroe: Yes, backup snapshots can be region-locked for Dedicated and Private. Hosted backups are also region-scoped when you pick an EU hosting option.
[11:24] Rina Alvarez: Can you give an example real audit scenario and how Redwood would assist? Say a regulator asks for logs from last 18 months for a particular customer.
[11:34] Priya Nair: If you have an 18-month retention on Dedicated with backups, Redwood can help produce the logs and a redaction audit trail. For Hosted, if data wasn't retained that long, we can produce what we have plus attestations. We also provide procedural support and an incident response pack.
[11:49] Ethan Boyle: About change management — do you support signed approvals for model rollouts and RBAC gating?
[11:55] Jordan Li: Yes, we have workflow support for approvals in the console and integration hooks for external ticketing systems. Approvals are stored in the audit trail.
[12:06] (longer section omitted in transcript but discussed: SCIM, SSO, personnel bindings)
[18:05] Marcus Chen: Quick question on network egress logs — do you record destination IPs for outbound calls from runtime for third-party tools?
[18:13] Priya Nair: We can record egress metadata and destination endpoints, but body payloads are avoided. For Private that remains in your control.
[20:02] Sofia Marin: Our compliance team will want to see the operator access matrix — who at Redwood has break-glass access in emergencies?
[20:10] Alex Monroe: We will provide a list and we have a documented break-glass process that requires approvals and is audited. For Private we can lock down that access more strictly.
[23:00] (conversation about encryption of caches, ephemeral keys, and implementation details.)
[29:10] Rina Alvarez: For HIPAA specifically, what is Redwood's approach to PHI in prompts?
[29:18] Priya Nair: We recommend isolating PHI flows to Dedicated or Private, enabling a BAA, using CMKs, and enforcing strict routing and retention. We also provide instrumentation for monitoring PHI exposures and can run periodic scans.
[30:05] Marcus Chen: If we go Private, what telemetry is still sent to Redwood for billing and support?
[30:12] Jordan Li: Minimal telemetry only if you opt in — e.g., metrics for subscriptions. We can operate in a support-forward but telemetry-minimal fashion; billing can be done via aggregated usage uplinks.
[31:00] Alex Monroe: Ok, let's do a quick recap and next steps. We'll send the compliance pack (SOC2, BAA template), a pricing sketch for Dedicated, and propose dates for a security deep-dive. Marcus to confirm PII dataset list. Priya will prepare the sizing report.
[31:20] Marcus Chen: Sounds good.
[31:24] Rina Alvarez: We'll want the BAA language to cover our HIPAA requirements; expect comments.
[31:30] Sofia Marin: And include examples of redaction audit logs please.
[31:34] Priya Nair: Will do.
[31:36] Alex Monroe: Anything else?
[31:38] Ethan Boyle: No, that's it.
[31:40] Alex Monroe: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the sec-deep dive.
